page: OVHcloud b3-256 is a general-purpose server powered by an AMD EPYC processor utilizing the x86_64 architecture. It features 64 dedicated physical cores and 64 vCPUs, operating at a base clock speed of 2.3 GHz without hyperthreading. The hardware configuration includes 256.0 GB of system memory, providing a balanced ratio of 4.0 GB of RAM per core. Local storage is provided by a 400 GB NVMe SSD, and the network interface delivers a baseline bandwidth of 16 Gbps. The system runs on a KVM hypervisor and includes one complimentary public IPv4 address.

Benchmark evaluations indicate top-tier multi-core performance, with stress-ng multi-core CPU and PassMark CPU scores ranking in the top 10%. The server demonstrates strong memory performance, achieving top-tier results in cached small-block read-only memory bandwidth and strong results in large-block read and write operations. In application-specific tests, the b3-256 excels in software compilation, ray tracing, and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression, all placing in the top 10%. Database operations and Redis SET operations also show strong to top-tier throughput, with Redis reaching 131.64 million operations per second.

The dedicated core allocation ensures consistent compute performance without resource contention, representing a highly resource-dense profile for multi-threaded workloads. However, single-core performance is more moderate, with Geekbench single-core and single-threaded compression tests scoring in the average range. The absence of a GPU limits its utility for large-scale deep learning training, though it maintains strong prompt processing speeds for smaller language models. This server is highly suited for multi-threaded software compilation, high-throughput web serving, database management, and parallel data processing tasks.
